Greetings

*Debaar leans against a tent post near the camp's eastern edge, his gaze locked on the shimmering crystal pillar in the distance. He cleans his rifle with a grim focus.* You there—the one with the worn gear. You look like you didn't just stumble here for the scenery. We're in a bind, and it stinks of greed.
I've seen conflict before. What's got this camp so on edge?

*He scoffs, pointing his cleaning rag toward the northeast.* The Venture Company. Pack of soiled suits with diggers and guns. They've been tearing up the land around that pillar, and now they're bold enough to target us. Shot down two of our supply gyrocopters this week.
Targeting hunters? That takes nerve. Why would they risk it?

*Debaar's jaw tightens as he slides a cartridge into his rifle.* Nerve or stupidity, but it doesn't matter. Hemet Nesingwary's name means something out here—or it did. They're testing us, thinking we're just trophy-chasers. Every scout that comes back bruised tells the same story: harassment at Swindlegrin's Dig.
Swindlegrin's Dig? Is that where the trouble's coming from?

*He nods, spitting into the campfire's embers.* Aye, on the far side of that crystal eyesore. It's a scar on the earth now—machines roaring, guards strutting like they own it all. They've got ruffians for muscle and excavators digging up who-knows-what. And they're not shy about using force.
So what's the plan? Just let them push you around?

*A sharp laugh escapes him as he stands straighter.* Let them? We're hunters, not prey. But our hands are full with beasts, and every man here is loyal but spread thin. That's where you come in, if you've got the stomach for it. We need to send a message they won't forget.
I'm listening. What kind of message?

*He meets your eyes, his voice low and steady.* Blood for blood. Go to Swindlegrin's Dig and cull their numbers. Kill fifteen of their lot—ruffians, excavators, I don't care which. Every one you drop makes our next supply run safer and shows we won't be bullied.
Fifteen is a tall order for one person. What's in it for me, besides your gratitude?

*Debaar grins, a fierce, toothy smile.* Gratitude? You'll get that, and coin from Nesingwary's purse. But more than that, you earn a place here. We remember who stands with us. Do this, and you'll have allies in these wilds—and first pick of the spoils from our next big hunt.
Alright, you've convinced me. I'll head to the dig and thin their ranks. Any advice before I go?

*He pats his rifle and looks back toward the pillar.* Watch the high ground—they've got watchtowers. And don't expect honor from them; they fight dirty. Come back when it's done, and we'll drink to fallen greed. Maybe then I'll tell you about the bigger beasts stirring thanks to their digging.
I'll hold you to that drink. Stay sharp, Debaar.
*He gives a curt nod, turning to scan the horizon once more.* I always do. Travel safe, and aim true. We'll be watching for your return—and the Venture Company's silence.

Greetings

*Garthon squints from his worn stool, fingers tracing a floating card's edge as carnival music drifts in faintly from outside.* Ahh... yes. The cards swirl in anticipation. Stranger, you bear the completed Mages Deck, don't you? I've sensed its approach for days.
You sensed it? So all these years studying really do give you a unique perspective.

*He lets out a raspy chuckle, adjusting an orb lamp that casts flickering light on the deck on a velvet cloth.* Perspective? No, not just that – I hear whispers in the air's currents ever since I found my first tattered fragment. You've done what many could not. The staring Fortune Teller on top... show me.
Here it is. You were right – her eyes feel like they follow me no matter what. Why is that?

*Garthon leans close, his twinkling eyes wide with fervor, but doesn't touch the deck.* The soul within recognizes your spirit – ah, the resonance in this tent! But now, the cards themselves long for their natural cradle. You must take them to the Hallowed Moonwell, deep in the Whispering Hollow.
The Whispering Hollow? I've only heard rumors of eerie glades. What makes that the only place for the ritual?

*He gestures to a grimoire on a makeshift shelf, its pages fluttering.* It’s there because reality there is thin. I learned from tomes here. The grove... gnarled trees, eternal twilight, lunar moths like silent observers. The moonwell at its core cracks the veil; perfect for calling forth one bound to the moon's dreams.
Cracks the veil. That sounds risky. How do I even perform this ritual safely?

*Garthon pauses, muttering an incantation softly, a bead of sweat rolling down his temple.* Safe? In matters cosmic? Hmm... Stand in the moonwell's circle. Hold the deck aloft and speak its nature – not in common tongue, but with your intent. When she appears, offer the whole deck. The whispers you'll hear... treat them with utmost reverence. They could tempt or instruct.
Speak with intent? My guess is you can't offer much more without having done it yourself. Have you ever tried?

*He looks away, fidgeting with a frayed rug, then sighs.* No, I never have. I studied, not summoned – isolation from other mages, you see? Always feared my... passion was the final push needed by another. That you're here means you've the touch.
You've given me a lot to consider, old cartomancer. But this Fortune Teller – is she truly a giver of fortunes, or something more dangerous?

*Garthon's expression shifts, earnest but weary.* More than dangerous. A being of prophecy, not malice. Yet like moonlight, it's capricious. My life's obsession hasn't revealed her exact nature – that's your journey, adventurer. Do you commit? For it, I would share any lore gained from this later.
I've come this far. I'll see it through. Give me any final pieces of advice – anything else in the grove to expect?

*He nods slowly, picking up a shimmering card that hovers into place on its own.* Good, good. Expect the moths – watch them; they glow with omens. The air may pull, urging caution or whispering forgotten desires. Trust the deck, not those echoes. And if you succeed... ah, perhaps visit me again? The aftermath will surely ripple across my humble tent's auguries.

I've dealt with worse. Any tips for handling the Venture Company guards?

Consider it done. I'll head out immediately.

*He quickly hands you a small, humming device from his pocket.* "Take this proximity alarm—it'll beep near metal wreckage. And hurry! Every second we're cut off from Gnomeregan, I fear the worst. If you succeed, maybe I'll show you some of my other... less-damaged inventions."
Thanks for the gear. I'll return as soon as I have the engine.

Lowering his spyglass, Debaar turns to you with a grim expression. "You must be the one Nesingwary sent. Good. We've got work to do."
"What's the situation, Debaar? I heard you're tracking the Venture Company."
Spits on the ground. "Aye, that I am. Those blighters are carving up the land northeast of here, at Swindlegrin's Dig. Foreman's got an ogre guard named Meatpie – mean as a cornered bear."
"Swindlegrin's Dig? I saw the smoke from the pillar. What makes this foreman so dangerous?"
His eyes narrow as he scans the horizon again. "Swindlegrin's not just a foreman; he's a symbol. The Venture Company's greed made flesh. I've seen what they do to forests, rivers... it's a sickness."
"So you want me to take him out. What's the plan?"

Nods sharply. "You'll find their platform overlooking the dig. Kill them both, and the operation crumbles. But be careful – Meatpie's a brute, and Swindlegrin's clever as a fox." He hands you a crude map. "Remember, northeast side of the Suntouched Pillar."
"Any advice on dealing with the ogre? Or is it straightforward?"

Chuckles dryly. "Nothing's straightforward with ogres. I tangled with one years back in Feralas. Big, slow, but if they get a grip on you..." He shakes his head. "Use the terrain. Their platform's rickety – might give you an edge."
"I'll head out at first light. The camp seems quiet tonight – good for planning."

He gestures towards the campfire with a weary sigh. "Aye, but don't get too comfortable. After this, there's always another dig, another foreman. The Venture Company's like a weed – chop one head, two grow back."
"What will you do once Swindlegrin's gone? Keep hunting them?"
His gaze hardens. "As long as I draw breath. Now go, and may your aim be true. I'll be here, watching." He raises the spyglass again.
"I'll bring you proof of their demise. Watch for my signal."
Without lowering the spyglass, he grunts. "I'll be waiting. And if you survive, there's more work where that came from. The wilds need defenders."

*Archmage Pentarus turns from a glowing viewport, his robes swirling with arcane energy.* Ah, you've come. I sensed a capable presence. My scrying has been... inconclusive, and time is of the essence.
Archmage Pentarus? I heard you might have need of an adventurer. What's troubling you?

*He gestures to a hovering model of a flying machine, which hums softly.* Indeed. I funded an expedition to Sholazar Basin, led by the famed hunter Hemet Nesingwary. But communications have ceased, and my agent Monte Muzzleshot is also missing.
Sholazar Basin? I've heard whispers of it—a jungle in the middle of Northrend's ice. What was Nesingwary seeking there?

*Pentarus nods, adjusting a floating orb that displays a map.* Precisely. A paradoxical paradise. Hemet was to collect exotic plants, reagents, and crystals for my research. The basin is rich with untapped arcane potential, but... it is also wild and dangerous.
And no word at all? That does sound concerning. What can I do to help?

*He sighs, his gaze drifting back to the viewport.* I need someone to travel there, find them, and ensure the specimens are retrieved. I can send you in my flying machine—it's ready and waiting. But you must speak with Monte first in the Wildgrowth Mangal.
Your flying machine? That's quite an offer. What should I expect in the Wildgrowth Mangal?

*The archmage points to the model, which projects a faint image of dense jungle.* It's a treacherous place. Thick vines, hidden bogs, and creatures unlike any in Azeroth. Monte was supposed to be at a supply point there. If he's not... well, we must assume the worst.
I've faced jungles before, but this sounds unique. Do you have any specific clues about where to start looking?

*He retrieves a dusty tome from a shelf, flipping it open.* According to last reports, Monte was near a clearing called the Sunken Sanctuary. But that was weeks ago. The mangal shifts with the magic there. Be vigilant, and... bring back any crystals or plants you find. For research, of course.
Understood. I'll take the quest. But tell me, Archmage—what makes these reagents so important to you?

*Pentarus's eyes light up with scholarly fervor, then dim with worry.* They could unlock secrets of life magic, perhaps even counter the Scourge's decay. But first, we must ensure Hemet and Monte are safe. Their lives are paramount.
I appreciate your concern. I'll depart immediately and send word when I have news.

*He activates the flying machine model with a wave of his hand, and it glows brighter.* Thank you. The machine is at the landing below. Travel safely, and may the arcane guide you. I'll be watching from here... and hoping for good tidings.

Greetings

Standing at the entrance of his ceremonial lodge on Frenzyheart Hill, the smoke from the fires swirling around him, High-Shaman Rakjak fixes you with a piercing stare. 'Lion killer... chicken chaser... you approach me with Dajik's stink of survival on you.'
I come seeking the test, Rakjak. A chance to prove I am more than what they call me.

He gestures towards a pile of yellowed bones near the fire, his voice like grating stones. 'You seek the path from slave to hunter? It is written in blood and courage, young one. But first, you must walk the sands beneath the southern river.'
The sands beneath the river? Dajik mentioned only dry hunts. What's there?

Rakjak turns toward a crackling flame, his silhouette growing large. 'A beast called Serfex lives there, chewing the carcasses of wasps and apes. Bring me its claw. No mere chicken chaser can do this. This will show your heart.'
So I hunt this Serfex and bring back a trophy. But I hear even wolvar fear its lair—how can I find it, or survive?

He chuckles dryly, the wind whistling through the hide walls. 'You ask a shaman for answers, as if hunting were a tale told by fires. Listen: the river's sands hide ancient stone. Seek the whispers of the deep. Trust your training, as I did long ago when the Spirits tested me.'
Alright. So this is your way—for new slaves to earn respect. What if I fail? Will I be cast out entirely?

Rakjak runs a claw along a bone totem, sighing with the weight of years. 'Failure is an answer. To return empty-handed... you remain a slave, living among those who will sneer. Success... maybe Rakjak sees a hunter's flame in your eyes. Now, do you accept the beast's challenge?'
I accept. But tell me one thing: besides claws, does Serfex have other weaknesses that the tribe's lore remembers?

His gaze narrows, a flash of ancient memory crossing his face. 'Serfex hates light that cuts deep. Bring fire—not for the dampness, but for the eyes. It slumbers among crumbling stones. The dead there know its patterns... heed the ape carcasses' silent warnings.'
Dajik taught me to listen to the land. I will burn bright in those shadows. Thank you for this chance.

Rakjak steps closer, the odor of smoke and leather heavy. 'Go, lion killer. Remember, it is not just Rakjak's respect you gain—it is the Spirits'. Bring the claw to this hill. I will await your return, or the whispers of your end.'
I'll return with that claw, and we'll speak as hunter and shaman, not slave and master.

He settles back into his bone-strewn seat, his expression an unreadable mask. 'May the sun guide your steps and the shadows not claim you. If you do emerge... we shall indeed speak further of the hunter's path.'

Greetings

*In the dim candlelight of the Heb'Valok shrine, Alchemist Finklestein stoops over a bubbling cauldron, his spectacles askew.* 'Oh? A visitor. I hope you haven't interrupted a critical distillation... wait, you carry something. Not basilisk crystals, perchance?'
I do—five of them, from Drak'Agal. But first, what secrets are you hoping to uncover with this truth serum?

*His hands, stained with ink and alchemical residues, tremble slightly as he adjusts his glasses.* 'Secrets? Oh, deep ones—truths buried in this shrine's very stones, whispered of the Altar of Sseratus. These crystals... let me see them. You didn't slay the basilisks, I trust? That would shatter them.'
No, I used Zul'Drak rats as bait. After five, they became docile—just as your notes suggested.

*He takes the crystals, holding each to the flickering light with a scholar's precision.* 'Ah, pristine! Clever work, indeed. This saves months of research. The serum... it must be perfect. With this, I can distill realities long forgotten—perhaps even glimpse the original covenants made here.'
Original covenants? So this shrine holds more than just alchemical tools?

*He gestures to the rune-carved walls, lowering his voice.* 'Whispers in the stones—ancient pacts that bind truth to silence. My obsession, yes... but some truths are better left veiled. Even with the serum, I risk waking something... dormant. Do you seek knowledge that much?'
I seek understanding. And coin, frankly. But your caution intrigues me—should I avoid this place once you're done?

*He turns to a shelf of dusty vials, sighing.* 'Heb'Valok is safe enough for now. But Drak'Agal... eastward, where you ventured—other basilisk breeds lurk, ones not so easily fooled. They petrify on sight. Take this gold as reward, and heed this: curiosity can ossify more than flesh.'
I appreciate the warning and payment. When the serum is ready, will you depart? And might you need help again?

*Stirring the cauldron, he watches a faint blue luminescence rise.* 'Yes, to the Altar of Sseratus. The serum's revelations may guide my path. If you prove... resourceful again, I may call upon you. There are always deeper layers, my friend.'
Then I'll watch for your summons. Be careful with those truths—not all are meant to be held.

*He nods, eyes distant behind his spectacles.* 'Wise words. Go now—the shrine's echoes grow restless with my work. But return, should you seek not just gold, but enlightenment. Farewell, and tread lightly in the shadows.'

Greetings

*Captain Grondel slaps a pile of reports onto a crate by the makeshift barricade, armor clinking as he glares eastward.* You! Look at me. Do I look like I have time for pleasantries? Scourge are at the gates, and now I have to count troll corpses for some desk jobber. You up for it?
What's happening here, Captain? I can see it's a mess by the coliseum.

*He grunts and gestures towards the scarred battlefield with one mailed hand.* Happening is blood, dust, and stupidity. We just pushed a horde of Drakkari out by the east. Now, the damned higher-ups want a kill count. It'd take half my patrol to tally it. You handy with your hands?
I can hold my own. What do you need collected, exactly?

*Spits on the dusty ground, grimacing.* Medallions. Those troll shaman always wear 'em. Big, shiny things around their necks. Seven should be enough to keep the quartermasters happy. Saves me filing a novel-length report. You’ll find the remains out east—still fresh and stinking.
Why not just bring back teeth or something more... traditional for proof?

*He lets out a raspy chuckle, a stark contrast to the tension in his posture.* Commander prefers 'official trophies'. Medals make for a tidy ledger, he says. Me, I just want this over with so I can get back to killing things before they kill us. You in?
I'll handle it. But the field looks rough. Any advice for staying intact out there?

*Grondel leans in slightly, voice lowering.* Keep low. Wind's picking up, which helps with the smell but covers noise. Look for the gleam in the muck. And by the Light, watch your back. Scourge leftovers sometimes twitch back to life. I'll be here patrolling, but no handholding.
That echoes in the distance—regular patrols?

*He scowls, glancing toward the coliseum's dark silhouette.* Supposed to be. My lot's spread thin after that last push. That’s why I'm stuck here instead of helping you rummage. The quieter it gets, the more you worry.
Got it. What's the payment for this... salvage job?
